title: Director of Strategic Sourcing

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: While 3M manufactures protective films in-house, the Director of Strategic Sourcing would evaluate strategic supplier relationships for raw materials, specialty polymers, and potential co-branding opportunities that could enhance 3M's product portfolio. Given Tedlar's 60+ years of proven performance and superior durability claims (12-20+ years vs 8-9 years for 3M's best overlaminates), this role would assess whether incorporating DuPont Tedlar films into select 3M product lines could strengthen 3M's competitive position in ultra-premium segments where customers demand maximum longevity and lowest total cost of ownership. They would care about Tedlar's ability to reduce warranty claims, lower customer complaints about premature degradation, and enable 3M to offer extended warranty programs beyond their current MCS warranty terms. With 3M's recent product launches like the Protection Wrap Film Color Series and extensive installer training networks, Strategic Sourcing would evaluate whether a strategic partnership with DuPont could differentiate 3M's offerings in high-performance architectural panels (competing with DI-NOC), transit interiors requiring extreme durability, or specialized anti-graffiti applications where Tedlar's easy-clean properties exceed 3M's current 8588G/8590M capabilities. Their KPIs around supplier innovation, cost optimization, and strategic partnerships make them relevant for exploring collaborative opportunities rather than pure competitive positioning.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: The Director of Strategic Sourcing at 3M owns vendor evaluation, supplier relationship strategy, and material sourcing decisions that impact product quality and cost structure. They assess whether external partnerships or material inputs can enhance 3M's competitive position without cannibalizing core manufacturing capabilities. This role likely reports to VP of Supply Chain or Chief Procurement Officer and influences cross-functional stakeholders including Product Development, R&D, and Business Unit leaders. Their authority extends to evaluating strategic co-development or licensing opportunities when external technologies offer clear differentiation advantages in target market segments.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Given 3M's existing product portfolio gaps, Tedlar would be most relevant for ultra-premium architectural graphics and building wraps where customers demand performance beyond 3M's current 8-9 year durability ceiling, transit and rail interiors requiring extreme temperature tolerance and mold resistance that exceeds standard vinyl capabilities, and specialized anti-graffiti applications for municipalities or high-vandalism environments where Tedlar's easy-clean properties (spray paint and permanent markers wipe off) outperform 3M's 8588G/8590M anti-graffiti overlaminates. These use cases would allow 3M to capture premium segments where warranty length and total cost of ownership drive purchasing decisions, without competing with 3M's core vehicle wrap and general signage product lines.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: This role's performance is measured by supplier innovation contribution to product roadmap, cost optimization across material inputs, and strategic partnerships that enhance competitive positioning. They personally care about identifying technologies that reduce warranty claim exposure, enable product line extensions into higher-margin segments, and strengthen 3M's market leadership against emerging competitive threats. With 3M actively launching new products like the Protection Wrap Film Color Series, they face pressure to ensure 3M's material sourcing strategy supports differentiation in premium markets where durability expectations are increasing. Tedlar's proven field performance and graffiti resistance could solve specific pain points around warranty costs and customer complaints in applications where 3M's current overlaminates underperform.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: 3M's recent Protection Wrap Film Color Series launch (2024 promotion through December) signals active product innovation cycles where strategic sourcing decisions are being evaluated. The company's extensive presence at ISA Sign Expo and PRINTING United as exhibitors and technology providers creates natural touchpoints for strategic partnership discussions. Additionally, 3M's ongoing management of their comprehensive MCS Warranty program means they're continuously monitoring warranty claim rates and performance data that could reveal opportunities where Tedlar's superior durability reduces risk exposure in specific application segments.

personalization_hooks.hook: 3M's current overlaminate portfolio tops out at 8-9 year outdoor durability claims while premium architectural projects increasingly demand performance specifications beyond this threshold
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Position Tedlar as a strategic gap-filler for ultra-premium segments where 3M could capture higher margins by offering extended warranty programs that current in-house materials cannot support. Frame this as portfolio enhancement rather than replacement of core products.

personalization_hooks.hook: 3M's anti-graffiti products (8588G, 8590M) require sacrificial layers or specific cleaning protocols, while municipalities and transit authorities increasingly demand graffiti solutions where vandalism cleans off with standard methods
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Open with empathy about the complexity of graffiti protection in high-vandalism environments, then introduce Tedlar's easy-clean properties as a potential co-development opportunity for municipal and transit applications where maintenance simplicity drives procurement decisions.

personalization_hooks.hook: Strategic Sourcing at 3M would evaluate whether external partnerships strengthen competitive position without cannibalizing core manufacturing, especially in niche applications where material performance determines warranty exposure
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Frame initial conversation as a confidential strategic discussion about selective market segments where DuPont and 3M could explore collaboration, emphasizing how Tedlar's field-proven performance could reduce warranty risk in applications that currently generate claims under MCS warranty programs.

recommended_approach: Lead with strategic partnership framing rather than supplier pitch—position this as a confidential exploration of selective market opportunities where Tedlar could complement (not compete with) 3M's core product lines. Emphasize specific applications like ultra-premium architectural projects or high-vandalism transit environments where 3M's current materials may be generating warranty costs or losing bids to competitors offering extended durability claims. Request a brief exploratory call to understand 3M's strategic priorities in these niche segments before proposing specific collaboration models.
